questions_and_answers.question_text: What does liáo mean, and what does tiān(r) do?
What does the le in Nǐ bié qù le tell you?
What is the literal meaning of yìtiān dào wǎn?
How may the phrase yìtiān dào wǎn be split up?
What are the two senses of péi?
Write the Chinese for "We chatted for an hour."
Write the Chinese for "He's busy all day long."

answers.answer_text: Tā yìtiān dào wǎn dōu zài máng.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "All our students here are very hardworking."

answers.answer_text: Wǒmen zhèrde xuésheng dōu hěn yònggōng.

questions_and_answers.question_text: What does yònggōng refer to specifically?

answers.answer_text: Being diligent or hardworking in one's studies.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "If no one goes along with me, I won't go."

answers.answer_text: Méi rén péi wǒ qù, wǒ jiù bú qù le.

articles.text:
3. A: Wǒ qù zhǎo Xiǎo Lán liáo      I'm going to go look for Xiǎo Lán to
      tiānr.                         have a chat.
   B: Nǐ bié qù le, tā yìtiān dào   Don't go, she works hard all day long
      wǎn yònggōng, méi shíjiān      and doesn't have the time to chat
      péi ni liáo tiānr.             with you.

Notes on No. 3

liáo tiān(r): "to chat." Liáo means "to chat," and tiān(r) acts as its object. Tiān(r) may also be omitted.

Wǒmen liáole yíge zhōngtóu.      We chatted for an hour.

Nǐ bié qù le: "don't go." The one syllable LE tells you that not going is a CHANGE from what was earlier expected. The translation might be "Change your plans and don't go."

yìtiān dào wǎn: "all day long." The syllable yī ("one") is sometimes used to mean "the whole, the entire." Yìtiān dào wǎn can be literally translated as "the whole day until late," but is also often used to mean "all the time, always." You can use the whole phrase as a time-when word, or you can SPLIT IT UP with a verb, as in yìtiān máng dào wǎn, "busy all day long."

Tā yìtiān dào wǎn dōu zài máng.  He's busy all day long.

yònggōng: "to be diligent, to be hardworking" in one's studies.

Wǒmen zhèrde xuésheng dōu hěn    All our students here are very
yònggōng.                        hardworking.

péi: "to accompany; to keep somebody company." In the Transportation module, you saw péi meaning "to accompany, to go along with." Here you see péi used in another sense, "to keep someone company."

Méi rén péi wǒ qù, wǒ jiù bú qù  If no one goes along with me, I won't
le.                              go.
Lǎo rén chángcháng xǐhuan yǒu    Older people often like to have someone
rén péizhe ta shuō huà.          to keep them company and talk with them.
